objective: Question 9 of the knot intuition asks which law, not written on a space in advance, gives a shape that looks like a space of low dimension. Re-posed at the base under the no-selection framing: what does the native gluing of knots build, and which laws see only that? Hypothesis under test: hub-free networks of three-place knots, where every shared distinction joins exactly two knots, glue into compact surfaces while two-place relations glue only into lines and loops; parity is the only knot whose glued result depends only on the surface, and its hidden witness bits count the genus. Nearest known work: pants decompositions, two-dimensional topological field theories (commutative Frobenius algebras) and Frobenius objects in the category of relations (groupoids, Heunen, Contreras and Cattaneo 2013; Mehta and Zhang 2020). Standalone value: which Boolean three-place relations glue topologically, which knots can build the surface-seeing knot without hubs, and the reading of the two/three boundary as the boundary between dimension one and dimension two.
status: Complete 2026-10-24: space from a law. Native gluing of three-place knots builds compact orientable surfaces (two-place relations only lines and loops); exactly four knots see only the surface with counts, the parity and Fibonacci fusion rules (one hidden bit per handle; Verlinde dimensions 2, 5, 15, 50); hub-free gadgets never create parity. Next: dimension three through hubs, deferred to the owner.
title: Space from a law: what native gluing builds
